title: RO-MT082-RoleInjectionEngine

scope.summary:
GOAL: Implement the per-transport Role Injection Engine: given an ACTIVE hsk.handshake_role@1 (MT-081) and a session launch, inject the role overlay through the correct transport-specific mechanism — Claude CLI, Codex CLI, or ACP — and record a typed injection event. Field-verified injection strategies (never full system-prompt replacement, which destroys the harness's agentic scaffolding): Claude = --append-system-prompt-file (overlay on top of defaults; the documented "You are a security engineer" pattern) with optional --agents '<json>' named-agent strategy; Codex = no append flag exists, so the role text is prepended to the first turn/start input under a stable delimiter contract; ACP = no system-prompt primitive, so the harness owns injection as the first session/prompt segment.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/role_injection.rs (RoleInjectionEngine + per-transport strategy impls + temp-overlay-file lifecycle), small integration seams into the launch paths delivered by MT-021 (Claude launch preset), MT-043 (Codex turn/start), MT-061 (ACP core), a new Flight Recorder event using the role-injection kind registered by MT-161's FR-kind catalog, plus tests. No frontend edits.

DETAILED SPEC:
- pub struct RoleInjectionEngine { store: HandshakeRoleStore, recorder: Arc<dyn FlightRecorder> } with pub async fn prepare_injection(&self, role_id, role_version: Option<u32>, transport: RoleTransport) -> Result<PreparedRoleInjection, RoleInjectionError>.
- pub enum RoleTransport { ClaudeCli, CodexCli, Acp } and pub enum PreparedRoleInjection with per-transport payloads:
  * ClaudeAppendFile { overlay_path: TempOverlayFile, extra_args: Vec<String> } — writes overlay_prompt to a mode-restricted temp file under the managed runtime temp root, yields ["--append-system-prompt-file", <path>]. Optional ClaudeAgentsJson { agents_json: String, agent_name: String } strategy renders the role as a named agent definition (description/tools/model/permissionMode + body prompt) yielding ["--agents", <json>, "--agent", <name>] when transport_bindings.claude == AGENTS_JSON.
  * CodexFirstTurnPrefix { prefixed_input: fn(original: &str) -> String } — prepends the overlay under the stable delimiter contract: "<handshake-role id=\"{id}\" version=\"{v}\" sha256=\"{h}\">\n{overlay}\n</handshake-role>\n\n" + original first-turn/start input. Delimiter format is a frozen contract (tests pin exact bytes) so transcripts are machine-recoverable.
  * AcpFirstPromptSegment { segment: PromptSegment } — same delimiter contract emitted as the first session/prompt segment through the MT-061 ACP core.
- TempOverlayFile: RAII guard; file created with restrictive permissions in the session's managed temp dir, path registered with the process ledger, deleted on Drop AND on session-end/failure sweep (double cleanup path); never created inside the repo worktree.
- Injection event: every successful prepare+attach records the MT-161 FR kind (role_injected) with { role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, transport, strategy, session_id }. The sha256 must match the registry row (MT-081) — mismatch aborts injection with a typed error.
- Guard rails: the engine exposes NO code path that renders a --system-prompt (full replacement) argument; only active-status roles are injectable (draft/retired -> typed RoleInjectionError::RoleNotActive); overlay size cap (configurable, default 64 KiB) with typed error to protect first-turn budgets.
- Note on scope: this MT prepares and records injection payloads and wires them into the three launch seams; whole-session behavioral proof across live CLIs is MT-087.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-021 Claude launch preset seam and official_cli_bridge.rs (CliBridgeConfig.args_template + OfficialCliBridgeRuntime::render_args) to determine where extra role args join the rendered arg vector without violating the template validators.
2. Implement RoleTransport/PreparedRoleInjection/RoleInjectionError and the engine skeleton over HandshakeRoleStore.
3. Implement TempOverlayFile RAII with process-ledger registration and the session-end sweep hook; unit-test both cleanup paths (Drop and sweep after simulated crash).
4. Implement the Claude append-file strategy and the optional agents-json strategy behind transport_bindings.claude.
5. Implement the Codex first-turn prefix function with the frozen delimiter contract; pin exact-byte tests.
6. Implement the ACP first-prompt segment through the MT-061 session/prompt path.
7. Wire the FR role_injected event (MT-161 kind) with sha256 verification against the registry.
8. Negative tests: draft role rejected; sha mismatch rejected; oversized overlay rejected; assert no strategy ever emits "--system-prompt" as a standalone arg.
9. Integration test per transport seam with a stub spawner asserting final arg vector / first-turn bytes / first-segment bytes.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** except named IPC read surfaces
.GOV/** (role protocols are read-only source material; importer reads, never writes)
src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/** (no new tables in this MT)
acceptance_criteria: RoleInjectionEngine prepares Claude append-file injection: overlay bytes land in a temp file outside the repo worktree and the extra args are exactly ["--append-system-prompt-file", <path>] (or the agents-json pair when bound).
Codex strategy produces first-turn input prefixed with the frozen <handshake-role .../> delimiter block; exact-byte test pins the delimiter contract.
ACP strategy emits the same delimiter block as the first session/prompt segment via the MT-061 core.
TempOverlayFile is cleaned up on Drop AND by the session-end/failure sweep; a simulated-crash test proves no orphan overlay file survives the sweep.
Every injection records the MT-161 role_injected FR event with role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, transport, strategy, session_id; sha mismatch against the registry aborts with a typed error.
Draft and retired roles are not injectable (typed RoleNotActive error).
No engine code path can emit a full --system-prompt replacement argument (negative test + grep proof).
Overlay size cap enforced with typed error.
expected_tests: per-transport strategy unit tests (arg vector / first-turn bytes / first-segment bytes)
implementation_notes: official_cli_bridge.rs validates args_template shape (e.g. {prompt} placement); join role args through the documented seam rather than mutating templates ad hoc — see render_args and the template validators around lines 984-1067.

Claude specifics (verified): --append-system-prompt/--append-system-prompt-file overlay on top of the default system prompt; --agents '<json>' defines named agents (description/tools/model/permissionMode + body prompt); --agent <name> runs the whole session under that role; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md load via message flow (skipped by --bare), so the overlay file is the reliable role carrier.
Codex specifics (verified): no append flag; config.toml profiles + AGENTS.md + initial turn/start input are the only carriers — hence the first-turn delimiter contract.
ACP specifics (verified): no system-prompt primitive; the harness owns role injection in launch/first-prompt.
Temp overlay files must live under the managed runtime temp root (portability: no hardcoded drive paths) and be registered with the process ledger for sweep-based reclamation.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend injection engine MT; operator visibility comes from MT-085 (GUI) and the role_injected FR events (trace projection).

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal engine behind the launch flow; the operator-facing manual entries land with MT-085 (Role Manager GUI) and MT-086 (spawn role_id surface), which document injection behavior end-to-end.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.behavior: role injection at session launch (all three transports)
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1; role_injected FR kind (MT-161) is the Tier-1 evidence surface.

risk_if_missed: Roles exist in the registry but never reach a live session; steering stays manual prose pasted into prompts, unrecorded and unverifiable, and MT-083/086/087 have no injection substrate.

risks: RISK-1: Scaffolding destruction — a shortcut that swaps the whole system prompt (instead of appending) silently strips the harness's agentic behaviors; sessions look launched but degrade unpredictably.
RISK-2: Orphaned overlay temp files — crashed or cancelled launches leak role text onto disk outside cleanup, violating quiet-operation and leaving stale prompts that a later session could pick up.

RISK-3: Injected-bytes drift — the bytes written to the temp file / first turn differ from the approved registry version (encoding, truncation, template interpolation), so the operator-approved role is not what runs.
RISK-4: Delimiter collision — a task payload containing the literal delimiter string corrupts the Codex/ACP role framing and lets payload text masquerade as role authority.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): no full-replacement code path exists (closed enums + negative test + grep proof target).
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): TempOverlayFile RAII + process-ledger registration + session-end/failure sweep; simulated-crash test proves zero orphans.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): sha256 of prepared bytes verified against the registry row before attach; mismatch aborts; role_injected event records the hash for post-hoc audit.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): delimiter includes the per-injection sha256 attribute making spoofed blocks detectable; composition layer (MT-083) escapes literal delimiter sequences in payload text; exact-byte tests pin the contract.

research_provenance.source: Verified field research: Claude Code --append-system-prompt-file / --agents / --agent (role overlay pattern; full --system-prompt replacement REJECTED as it destroys agentic scaffolding; CLAUDE.md loads via message flow, skipped by --bare); Codex no-append-flag reality (AGENTS.md + config.toml profiles + first-turn input); ACP has no system-prompt primitive (harness-owned injection). Inspected product code: official_cli_bridge.rs CliBridgeConfig/args_template/render_args + template validators; operator_chat.rs OperatorChatLaunchService::build_spawn_request/launch; process ledger for cleanup registration.
corrections: Injection is append/prefix-only across all three transports; replacement is a contract-level forbidden action, not a style preference.
Codex and ACP get an identical frozen delimiter contract so transcripts remain machine-recoverable across providers.
Injection eventing depends on the MT-161 FR-kind catalog; this MT consumes, never invents, event kinds.
